title: Stabilize GPU stack: CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS compatibility and kernel refactor
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: Several customer incidents and CI flakes trace back to mismatches between CUDA toolkits, Triton runtime versions, and CUTLASS kernels. We have fragile ifdefs and ad-hoc workarounds in the serving runtime that cause silent correctness issues (mis-sized workspaces, occasional NaNs in fp16 paths) and large perf regressions when the system uses unexpected driver/runtime versions. This ticket scopes a surgical refactor and dependency upgrades to improve cross-version compatibility and reduce runtime branching. Goals: (1) Upgrade and pin tested CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS versions in CI images, (2) Refactor kernel registration and capability checks into a small compatibility layer, (3) Add deterministic smoke and perf tests to catch alignment/workspace regressions, (4) Provide graceful fallback paths for unsupported driver combinations.
acceptance_criteria: CI images updated to include CUDA 12.3 and 12.4 toolchains and at least Triton 2.21; images are documented in infra/ci-images.md
Runtime compiles cleanly against both CUDA 12.3 and 12.4 in CI matrices without compiler warnings turned into failures
New compatibility layer centralizes compute-capability checks and kernel selection; no remaining per-kernel #ifdefs in src/runtime/kernels/ except for clearly marked hardware intrinsics
Smoke correctness tests (small prompt generation, kv cache sanity, fp16 checksum) added and pass in CI on both native and containerized runners
Performance baselines collected pre/post change and show no >10% regression on p50 token latency for target models (llama-2-7B, llama-2-13B) on standard test harness
A canary rollout plan exists and is used to promote the new runtime images to dedicated and hosted pools with rollback metrics defined
technical_notes: Observed failures: mis-sized CUTLASS workspace when using tensorcore kernels compiled with NVCC flag -arch=sm_86 vs runtime device sm_80; fixed by harmonizing tile-size macro mapping and exporting tile metadata to the runtime registry
Triton ABI changes: symbol versioning in Triton 2.20+ requires updated dlopen behavior; implemented a thin loader that validates Triton ABI before binding
Pinned dependencies in third_party/ to CUTLASS 2.11.0, Triton v2.21.1, CUDA toolkit 12.4 for release branch; added script infra/bin/lock_gpu_deps.sh to recreate vendor builds

Refactor: introduce src/runtime/gpu/compat.h and gpu_compat.cc to encapsulate compute capability, workspace sizing, and kernel feature flags. Replace scattered checks across 24 files with calls into compatibility API

Added fallback: if a tensorcore kernel fails launch or reports invalid args, runtime will retry with compatible non-tensorcore kernel and emit metric 'gpu.kernel.fallback' with tags {model, kernel, reason}
CI: expanded matrix to run unit tests on ubuntu-22.04 with CUDA 12.3 & 12.4 and a smoke run on a Tesla A100 and an RTX 6000 to catch divergent driver behavior
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): build new runtime image and deploy to a dedicated canary pool (internal only) — 24h smoke + perf collection
Phase 2 (limited): promote to 5% of hosted traffic on non-urgent routes for 72h, monitor cpu/gpu memory errors, token latency p50/p95, and kernel.fallback metric
Phase 3 (ramp): 25% -> 50% over 48h windows if metrics are stable, otherwise immediate rollback
Rollback criteria: any increase in error rate >0.5% absolute, kernel.fallback rate >0.1% for production models, or p95 latency regression >15%
Post-deploy: run full perf benchmark suite and open a follow-up for any model-specific tuning (quantization or kernel selection)
test_plan: Unit tests for gpu_compat APIs (compute capability mapping, workspace computation) on x86 CI runners
Integration smoke: small generation through the runtime (1 request, 512 tokens) verifying output checksum matches golden for both CUDA 12.3 and 12.4 images
Regression harness: nightly perf run comparing baseline and candidate images for llama-2-7B and llama-2-13B using serving-loadbench
Chaos tests: simulated device/proc restarts during active requests to ensure fallback paths trigger and no memory leaks occur
GPU sanitizer job: run device memory leak detectors and check for illegal memory reads on a subset of kernels
